dimensions.assessment: Affects traveling parents carrying infant nutrition items, TSA personnel, and private security screening personnel.
dimensions.evidence: apply to security screening personnel of the Administration and personnel of private security companies providing security screening

dimensions.assessment: Improves hygienic handling and screening standards during security checks without fundamentally altering travel rights.
dimensions.evidence: minimize the risk for contamination of any breast milk, baby formula, purified deionized water for infants, and juice

dimensions.assessment: Requires an audit and report by the DHS Inspector General, but specifies no direct spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: the Inspector General of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit... a report containing an audit of compliance

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Bottles and Breastfeeding Equipment Screening Act by adding new guidance and audit requirements.
dimensions.evidence: The Bottles and Breastfeeding Equipment Screening Act (Public Law 114-293) is amended by adding at the end the following new sections

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing guidance requirements to be updated every five years, alongside a one-time IG audit.
dimensions.evidence: every five years thereafter, if appropriate, the Administrator of the Transportation Security Administration shall issue or update

missing_information: Exact cost of implementing updated screening procedures or conducting the Inspector General audit
importance_detail.rationale: Directs the TSA to issue and update guidance for hygienic screening of infant feeding accessories and requires a one-time DHS Inspector General audit, impacting airport screening procedures and traveling families.
